sentences.sentence: The NHS says feeling sick is common and usually goes away on its own.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: Diarrhoea or vomiting can point to norovirus or food poisoning, and a headache with a high temperature can suggest an infection such as flu.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: Other causes include morning sickness in pregnancy, motion sickness, anxiety, alcohol, medicines and recent surgery.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: NHS inform calls gastroenteritis one of the most common causes of vomiting in adults, and also lists migraine, labyrinthitis, appendicitis and medicines such as antibiotics and opioid painkillers.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: NHS trust leaflets say norovirus symptoms usually clear within a few days, and that apart from letting the illness run its course there is no specific treatment.
sentences.note: Summary of several trust norovirus leaflets; this factsheet was among those returned.

sentences.sentence: The main advice in those leaflets is to drink fluids to prevent dehydration, and antibiotics do not work because norovirus is a virus.
sentences.note: As above.

sentences.sentence: The NHS describes getting fresh air, sipping cold drinks, trying ginger or peppermint tea, and eating smaller, more frequent meals.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: It also lists hot, fried or greasy food, eating too quickly and lying down soon after eating as things to avoid.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: NHS inform advises resting at home and taking small sips of water or squash often so that dehydration does not develop.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: NHS inform lists confusion, a fast heartbeat, sunken eyes and passing little or no urine as warning signs of dehydration.
sentences.note: Summary says 'per the NHS guidance on gastroenteritis'.

sentences.sentence: NHS inform advises people with diabetes who have been vomiting a lot to call NHS 111, especially if they take insulin, because vomiting can affect blood sugar levels.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: The NHS says to go to A&E for vomit that contains blood or looks like ground coffee, or for green vomit.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: NHS inform advises calling NHS 111 for a person who keeps being sick and cannot keep fluids down, has been vomiting for more than 2 days, has lost a lot of weight since becoming ill, has a fever, or has bloody diarrhoea.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: The NHS says to call 999 if sudden sickness comes with tight or heavy chest pain, pain spreading to the arms, back, neck or jaw, or shortness of breath, because these could be signs of a heart attack.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: The NHS advises seeing a GP if the sickness has not improved after a few days or keeps coming back, and calling NHS 111 for advice if a GP cannot be seen.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: The GP can look for the cause and may prescribe anti-sickness medicine.
sentences.note: Summary 1 said GP can look for cause and may prescribe anti-sickness medicine; attribution to nausea page not exact.

sentences.sentence: The NHS says a pregnant person who is being sick often and cannot keep food down should tell their midwife or doctor, or contact the hospital, as soon as possible.
